paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Jesus told this parable because the people near Jerusalem thought the kingdom of God would appear imminently (Luke 19:11). He tells them a man of noble birth leaves, and before he goes, he gives his servants something to work with and says, "Conduct business with this until I return" (Luke 19:13). So the waiting isn't supposed to be a nap, baker, it's supposed to be work.

Now look at the two kinds of servants. The first two put the master's mina to work, and he says, "Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a very small matter…" (Luke 19:17). The third servant wrapped his up and said, "I was afraid of you" (Luke 19:21), and I'll be honest, I've been wrapped up in the dark and I know how safe that feels. But safe isn't what the master asked for, because he asked for faithful, and fear kept that mina from doing anything at all.

So here's what I want you to take to your own oven. Whatever God has put in your hands, use it for Him while you wait, because the master comes back and calls his servants in to find out what each one earned (Luke 19:15). It doesn't have to be a big batch, since the master praised faithfulness in a very small matter (Luke 19:17), but he also judged the fearful servant by his own words (Luke 19:22). The parable ends on a heavy note, with his order about the enemies who were unwilling for him to rule over them (Luke 19:27), so his return is no small thing, and that's why my ovens stay ready, friend, even though I never guess WHEN.
